newsitem.title: USA: Sears faces class action lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Sears faces class action lawsuit.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck & Co. faces a class action lawsuit alleging the retailer and three officers misled investors by failing to disclose a credit card business practice that violated federal bankruptcy law, attorneys for the plaintiffs said Monday.

The lawsuit, filed in Chicago, follows Sears' admission this month that it did not properly file with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court some agreements to continue receiving payments from bankrupt holders of Sears' credit cards.
Sears allegedly misled many of its indebted credit card holders into believing they had to pay their bills, even though those debts had been nullified by a bankruptcy court.
Sears, the nation's second-largest retailer, said it would pay back millions of dollars in debt collected under the agreements and would also issue $100 gift certificates to card holders affected.
Last week the U.S. Attorney's office in Massachusetts filed a civil lawsuit against the company to stop the allegedly "fraudulent" debt collection activities.
The latest lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court in Chicago, names as defendants Sears, Chief Exectuive Arthur Martinez, Chief Financial Officer Alan Lacy and Controller James Blanda.
Sears also faces a continuing federal investigation in the matter, lawsuits by debtors and others by shareholders, and possible punitive damages in bankruptcy court.
Sears, which is based in Hoffman Estates, Ill., said last week it was cooperating in the probe by federal prosecutors.
Sears' stock fell 12.5 cents to $48.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
